Class Plane

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.geometry.Plane
public class Plane extends Object
A plane in three-dimensional Cartesian space.

The plane is stored in the form a*x + b*y + c*z = d. It can also be viewed as (r - r0) dot n = 0, where r0 is a point on the plane and n = (a, b, c) is a normal vector. The sign of the signed distance is positive on the side pointed to by the normal.

Author:
heddle

  • Constructor Details

    • Plane

      public Plane(Vector anorm, Point p0)
      Creates a plane from a normal vector and a point on the plane.

      The stored normal is normalized to unit length.

      Parameters:
      anorm - the plane normal vector
      p0 - a point on the plane
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if either argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if either argument contains non-finite values, or the normal is too close to zero to normalize

    • Plane

      public Plane(double a, double b, double c, double d)
      Creates a plane from the coefficients of a*x + b*y + c*z = d.
      Parameters:
      a - the x coefficient
      b - the y coefficient
      c - the z coefficient
      d - the right-hand side coefficient
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a coefficient is non-finite, or if a, b, and c are all too close to zero to define a plane

      public Plane(double[] norm, double[] point)

      Throws:

  • Method Details

    • interpolate

      public double interpolate(Point p1, Point p2, Point p)
      Creates a line through two points and computes the line-plane intersection.
      Parameters:
      p1 - one point defining the line
      p2 - another point defining the line
      p - upon return, contains the intersection point; set to NaN components if the line is parallel to the plane
      Returns:
      the line parameter t; NaN means the line is parallel to the plane. If 0 <= t <= 1, the finite segment intersects the plane. If t is outside [0, 1], the infinite line intersects the plane but the finite segment does not.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if any point argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if p1 and p2 are coincident or too close to define a stable line

    • lineIntersection

      public double lineIntersection(Line line, Point intersection)
      Computes the intersection of an infinite line with this plane.
      Parameters:
      line - the line to intersect with this plane
      intersection - upon return, contains the intersection point; set to NaN components if the line is parallel to the plane
      Returns:
      the line parameter t; NaN means the line is parallel to the plane. If 0 <= t <= 1, the finite segment intersects the plane. If t is outside [0, 1], the infinite line intersects the plane but the finite segment does not.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if either argument is null

    • sign

      public int sign(double x, double y, double z)
      Computes the side of the plane on which coordinates lie.
      Parameters:
      x - the x coordinate
      y - the y coordinate
      z - the z coordinate
      Returns:
      +1 if a*x + b*y + c*z > d, -1 if it is less than d, and 0 if it is exactly equal

    • constantPhiPlane

      public static Plane constantPhiPlane(double phi)
      Creates the vertical plane of constant azimuthal angle phi.

      The angle is measured in degrees in the usual xy-plane sense: phi = 0 is the positive x axis and phi = 90 is the positive y axis. The plane contains the z axis and the ray at the given azimuth.

      Parameters:
      phi - the azimuthal angle in degrees
      Returns:
      the plane of constant phi

    • planeQuadCoordinates

      public float[] planeQuadCoordinates(float scale)
      Computes four vertices that can be used to draw a quadrilateral patch of this plane.

      The returned array contains four xyz triples, suitable for JOGL-style vertex submission. The quadrilateral is not a mathematically bounded plane; it is a drawing convenience whose size is controlled by scale.

      Parameters:
      scale - a drawing scale, typically larger than the scene extent
      Returns:
      an array of twelve floats containing four xyz vertices
